decks.title: Ratio and Proportion — Part 1: Ratios, proportion and proportionals
goals: Form duplicate, triplicate, sub-duplicate, sub-triplicate, reciprocal and compound ratios
Test whether four numbers are in proportion and find the fourth proportional
Find the mean proportional and the third proportional
Work with numbers in continued proportion

slides.heading: Ratio and Proportion, Part 1
slides.body_md: A ratio compares two quantities; a proportion says two ratios are equal.

visual.alt: Table: the ratio 12 to 18 simplifies to 2 to 3; the proportion 2 to 3 equals 8 to 12 because 2 times 12 and 3 times 8 are both 24; the numbers 4, 6 and 9 are in continued proportion because 6 squared and 4 times 9 are both 36.
visual.caption: Ratio, proportion and continued proportion.

slides.narration: Welcome to ratio and proportion. A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind, such as twelve to eighteen, which simplifies to two to three. A proportion says that two ratios are equal. In this part you will meet new kinds of ratio, test proportions, and find missing proportionals.

slides.heading: What you will be able to do
slides.narration: These are your goals for part one. First the kinds of ratio built from a single ratio. Then proportion and its test: the product of the extremes equals the product of the means. Finally continued proportion, with the mean and third proportionals.

slides.heading: Kinds of ratio
slides.body_md: From one ratio $a : b$ (with $a, b > 0$) we can build several others:

visual.alt: Table of kinds of ratio for a to b: duplicate a squared to b squared, so 2 to 5 gives 4 to 25; triplicate a cubed to b cubed, 8 to 125; sub-duplicate takes square roots, 16 to 49 gives 4 to 7; sub-triplicate takes cube roots, 8 to 125 gives 2 to 5; reciprocal b to a, 5 to 2; compound with c to d is ac to bd, so 2 to 5 with 3 to 4 gives 3 to 10.
visual.caption: Six kinds of ratio built from $a : b$.

slides.narration: Squaring both terms gives the duplicate ratio; cubing gives the triplicate ratio. Square roots give the sub duplicate ratio, and cube roots the sub triplicate ratio. Swapping the terms gives the reciprocal ratio. Multiplying two ratios term by term gives their compound ratio. Always simplify the answer to lowest terms.

slides.heading: Why duplicate ratios matter
slides.body_md: If two squares have sides in the ratio $2 : 3$, their areas are in the ratio $4 : 9$.

visual.alt: Two squares drawn to scale side by side: the first has side 2 centimetres and area 4 square centimetres; the second has side 3 centimetres and area 9 square centimetres. The sides are in the ratio 2 to 3 and the areas in the ratio 4 to 9.
visual.caption: Sides $2 : 3$, areas $4 : 9$: areas are in the **duplicate ratio** of the sides.

slides.narration: Here is one place duplicate ratios appear. The sides of these squares are two and three centimetres. Their areas are four and nine square centimetres. So areas are in the duplicate ratio of the sides. In the same way, volumes of cubes are in the triplicate ratio of their edges.

slides.heading: Worked example 1: a compound ratio
slides.body_md: Find the compound ratio of the duplicate ratio of $3 : 4$ and the sub-duplicate ratio of $16 : 25$.

visual.alt: Working table: the duplicate ratio of 3 to 4 is 9 to 16; the sub-duplicate ratio of 16 to 25 is 4 to 5; multiplying term by term gives 36 to 80, which is 9 to 20 in lowest terms.
visual.caption: Find each ratio first, then multiply term by term.

slides.narration: Work out each ratio first. The duplicate ratio of three to four is nine to sixteen. The sub duplicate ratio of sixteen to twenty five is four to five. Now multiply first terms together and second terms together: thirty six to eighty. Divide both by four to get nine to twenty.

slides.heading: Quick check: duplicate ratio
slides.body_md: Square both terms.
slides.narration: Square each term of the ratio. Do not simply double them.

slides.heading: Proportion: extremes and means
slides.body_md: Four numbers $a, b, c, d$ are **in proportion**, written $a : b = c : d$ or $a : b :: c : d$, when $\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{c}{d}$. Then $a$ and $d$ are the **extremes**, $b$ and $c$ the **means**, and $ad = bc$.

visual.alt: Table for the proportion 4 to 7 equals 12 to 21: 4 and 21 are the extremes, 7 and 12 are the means; the product of the extremes, 84, equals the product of the means, 84.
visual.caption: In $4 : 7 = 12 : 21$, extremes $\times$ extremes $=$ means $\times$ means.

slides.narration: Four numbers are in proportion when the first two have the same ratio as the last two. The first and fourth are called the extremes, the second and third the means. Cross multiplying shows the test: the product of the extremes equals the product of the means. Here both products are eighty four.

slides.heading: A proportion on a graph
slides.body_md: Pairs with the same ratio lie on one straight line through the origin.

visual.alt: Graph of the straight line y equals 1.75 x through the origin. The points (4, 7), (8, 14) and (12, 21) all lie on it: each pair has the ratio 4 to 7, so any two of them form a proportion such as 4 to 7 equals 12 to 21.
visual.caption: Pairs in the same ratio lie on one line through the origin.

slides.narration: Plot each pair as a point. Four and seven, eight and fourteen, twelve and twenty one all lie on the same straight line through the origin, because each pair is in the ratio four to seven. Any two of these pairs make a proportion.

slides.heading: Worked example 2: testing and the fourth proportional
slides.body_md: (a) Are $1.2$, $2$, $4.8$ and $8$ in proportion? (b) Find the fourth proportional to $5$, $7$ and $15$.

visual.alt: Working table: for 1.2, 2, 4.8 and 8 the product of the extremes is 9.6 and the product of the means is 9.6, so they are in proportion; the fourth proportional to 5, 7 and 15 is 7 times 15 divided by 5, which is 21.
visual.caption: Equal cross-products mean the numbers are in proportion.

slides.narration: For part a, multiply the extremes, one point two and eight, to get nine point six. Multiply the means, two and four point eight, also nine point six. The products agree, so the numbers are in proportion. For part b, the fourth proportional x satisfies five to seven equals fifteen to x, so x is twenty one.

slides.heading: Quick check: fourth proportional
slides.body_md: Write the proportion with $x$ last.
slides.narration: Write four to ten equals six to x, then use the product of extremes and means.

slides.heading: Continued proportion
slides.body_md: Three numbers $a, b, c$ are in **continued proportion** when $a : b = b : c$. Then $b$ is the **mean proportional** between $a$ and $c$, and $c$ is the **third proportional** to $a$ and $b$.

visual.alt: Flow chart: a to b equals b to c gives b squared equals a times c; from this the mean proportional b is the square root of a c, and the third proportional c is b squared divided by a.
visual.caption: Continued proportion: one equation, two formulas.

slides.narration: In continued proportion the middle number is shared: a is to b as b is to c. Cross multiplying gives b squared equals a c. So the mean proportional is the square root of a c, and the third proportional is b squared divided by a.

slides.heading: The mean proportional as a square
slides.body_md: A rectangle $12$ cm by $3$ cm and a square of side $6$ cm have the same area.

visual.alt: A rectangle 12 centimetres by 3 centimetres and a square of side 6 centimetres, drawn to the same scale. Both have area 36 square centimetres, so the side of the square, 6, is the mean proportional between 12 and 3.
visual.caption: Equal areas: $12 \times 3 = 6 \times 6$, so $6$ is the mean proportional between $12$ and $3$.

slides.narration: Here is a picture of the mean proportional. A rectangle twelve by three has area thirty six. A square with the same area has side six. Six is the mean proportional between twelve and three, because twelve is to six as six is to three.

slides.heading: Worked example 3: mean and third proportionals
slides.body_md: Find (a) the mean proportional between $0.32$ and $0.5$ (b) the third proportional to $5$ and $7.5$.

visual.alt: Working table: the mean proportional between 0.32 and 0.5 is the square root of 0.16, which is 0.4; the third proportional to 5 and 7.5 is 7.5 squared, 56.25, divided by 5, which is 11.25.
visual.caption: Both answers come from $b^2 = ac$.

slides.narration: For the mean proportional, multiply the two numbers and take the square root: the product is zero point one six, and its square root is zero point four. For the third proportional, write five to seven point five equals seven point five to x. Then five x is fifty six point two five, so x is eleven point two five.

slides.heading: Worked example 4: finding an unknown term
slides.body_md: Find $x$ if $x - 1$, $x + 2$ and $x + 8$ are in continued proportion.

visual.alt: Table: with x equal to 4 the three terms are 3, 6 and 12, and 3 to 6 equals 6 to 12, both being 1 to 2, so they are in continued proportion.
visual.caption: Check: each term is twice the one before.

slides.narration: Use the rule that the square of the middle term equals the product of the other two. Expand both sides. The x squared terms cancel, leaving three x equals twelve, so x is four. The numbers are three, six and twelve, and each is twice the one before.

slides.heading: Quick check: mean proportional
slides.body_md: Multiply, then take the square root.
slides.narration: Multiply five by forty five, then find the square root of the product.

slides.heading: Four numbers in continued proportion
slides.body_md: $a, b, c, d$ are in continued proportion when $a : b = b : c = c : d$. For example $8, 12, 18, 27$ (common ratio $2 : 3$), and $a : d = 8 : 27$, the **triplicate** ratio of $a : b$.

visual.alt: Graph of the terms 8, 12, 18 and 27 against their positions 1 to 4, on the curve y equals 8 times 1.5 to the power x minus 1. Each term is 1.5 times the one before, so the four numbers are in continued proportion.
visual.caption: Four numbers in continued proportion: a common ratio of $1.5$.

slides.narration: Four numbers can be in continued proportion too. Eight, twelve, eighteen and twenty seven each grow by the same factor, one point five. The ratio of the first to the last, eight to twenty seven, is the cube of two to three: the triplicate ratio of the first two terms.

slides.heading: Quick check: continued proportion
slides.body_md: Test $b^2 = ac$ for each set.
slides.narration: For each set, square the middle number and compare it with the product of the other two.

slides.heading: Summary
bullets: Duplicate $a^2 : b^2$; triplicate $a^3 : b^3$; sub-duplicate and sub-triplicate use roots
Compound ratio: multiply term by term
Proportion: product of extremes $=$ product of means

rows: duplicate $a^2 : b^2$, triplicate $a^3 : b^3$, sub-duplicate $\sqrt{a} : \sqrt{b}$, sub-triplicate, reciprocal $b : a$, compound $ac : bd$
product of extremes $ad$ = product of means $bc$

visual.alt: Summary table for part 1: kinds of ratio; a proportion has equal products of extremes and means; the fourth proportional to a, b, c is b c over a; continued proportion means b squared equals a c; the mean proportional is the square root of a c; the third proportional to a and b is b squared over a.
visual.caption: Part 1 on one card.

slides.narration: To sum up part one. Duplicate and triplicate ratios square and cube the terms; sub duplicate and sub triplicate take roots. A compound ratio multiplies term by term. Four numbers are in proportion when the product of the extremes equals the product of the means. In continued proportion, the middle term squared equals the product of the outer terms.

slides.heading: Exam tips: how marks are awarded
bullets: **Show the test:** write both products, then conclude
**Mistake:** doubling instead of squaring for a duplicate ratio
**Mistake:** taking the third proportional in the wrong order
**Mistake:** leaving a ratio such as $36 : 80$ unsimplified
**Mistake:** giving the average instead of the mean proportional
slides.narration: In the exam, always write the proportion before solving it, because that line earns a mark. For a test of proportion, show both products and state your conclusion. Simplify every ratio to lowest terms. And remember: the mean proportional is a square root, not an average.

decks.title: Ratio and Proportion — Part 2: Properties of proportion and applications
goals: State and use invertendo, alternendo, componendo and dividendo
Use componendo and dividendo to solve equations and find ratios
Solve simple direct applications of proportion

slides.heading: Ratio and Proportion, Part 2
slides.body_md: One proportion gives five more, and one of them solves equations quickly.

nodes.label: Componendo and dividendo: $(a + b) : (a - b) = (c + d) : (c - d)$

visual.alt: Flow chart: from a to b equals c to d follow five properties: invertendo, b to a equals d to c; alternendo, a to c equals b to d; componendo, a plus b to b equals c plus d to d; dividendo, a minus b to b equals c minus d to d; and componendo and dividendo, a plus b to a minus b equals c plus d to c minus d.
visual.caption: Five properties of one proportion.

slides.narration: Welcome to part two. Starting from a single proportion, a is to b as c is to d, we can write five new proportions. They have Latin names: invertendo, alternendo, componendo, dividendo, and componendo and dividendo. The last one is a powerful tool for solving equations.

slides.heading: What you will be able to do
bullets: Find a ratio such as $x : y$ from an equation
slides.narration: These are your goals for part two. Learn the five properties and when to use each. Use componendo and dividendo to solve equations and find ratios. Prove relations by putting every term in terms of a common ratio k. Finally, apply proportion to simple problems.

slides.heading: Invertendo and alternendo
slides.body_md: If $a : b = c : d$, then **invertendo** gives $b : a = d : c$ and **alternendo** gives $a : c = b : d$ (swap the means).

visual.alt: Table for 7 to 4 equals 21 to 12: invertendo gives 4 to 7 equals 12 to 21, alternendo gives 7 to 21 equals 4 to 12; in every row the two cross-products are 84.
visual.caption: Each new proportion still has equal cross-products.

slides.narration: Invertendo turns both ratios upside down. Alternendo swaps the two middle terms, so the first is to the third as the second is to the fourth. With seven to four equals twenty one to twelve, both new proportions still have equal cross products, eighty four.

slides.heading: Componendo and dividendo
slides.body_md: **Componendo:** $(a + b) : b = (c + d) : d$. **Dividendo:** $(a - b) : b = (c - d) : d$. **Componendo and dividendo:** $(a + b) : (a - b) = (c + d) : (c - d)$.

visual.alt: Table for 7 to 4 equals 21 to 12: componendo gives 11 to 4 equals 33 to 12; dividendo gives 3 to 4 equals 9 to 12; componendo and dividendo gives 11 to 3 equals 33 to 9; each pair of cross-products is equal.
visual.caption: The new proportions from $7 : 4 = 21 : 12$.

slides.narration: Componendo adds the second term to the first in each ratio. Dividendo subtracts it. Componendo and dividendo combines them: the sum over the difference on one side equals the sum over the difference on the other. Check the table: every new proportion has equal cross products.

slides.heading: Why componendo and dividendo works
slides.body_md: Add $1$ to both sides, subtract $1$ from both sides, then divide the two results.

visual.alt: Flow chart: starting from a over b equals c over d, adding 1 to both sides gives componendo and subtracting 1 gives dividendo; dividing the first result by the second gives componendo and dividendo.
visual.caption: Why componendo and dividendo works.

slides.narration: Why does it work? Adding one to both sides of a over b equals c over d gives componendo. Subtracting one gives dividendo. Dividing the first result by the second cancels b and d, leaving componendo and dividendo. The steps can be reversed, so the property also works backwards.

slides.heading: Quick check: name the property
slides.body_md: Which terms were swapped?
slides.narration: Look at which two terms changed places, and recall the name of that property.

slides.heading: Worked example 1: solving an equation
slides.body_md: Solve $\dfrac{2x + 9}{2x - 9} = \dfrac{5}{3}$.

visual.alt: Graph of y equals 2x plus 9 over 2x minus 9 for x from 8 to 30, falling towards 1, and the horizontal line y equals five thirds. They meet at x equals 18, the solution of the equation.
visual.caption: The curve meets the line $y = \dfrac{5}{3}$ at $x = 18$.

slides.narration: Apply componendo and dividendo. On the left, the sum of numerator and denominator is four x and the difference is eighteen. On the right, five plus three over five minus three is four. So four x over eighteen is four, and x is eighteen. The graph confirms it: the curve meets the line at eighteen.

slides.heading: Worked example 2: finding a ratio
slides.body_md: If $\dfrac{5x + 3y}{5x - 3y} = \dfrac{7}{3}$, find $x : y$.

visual.alt: Working table: componendo and dividendo gives 10x over 6y equals 10 over 4; so x over y equals 3 over 2, that is x to y is 3 to 2; check: 21 over 9 equals 7 over 3.
visual.caption: The coefficients $5$ and $3$ must be divided out at the end.

slides.narration: Componendo and dividendo removes the y from the top and the x from the bottom: ten x over six y equals ten over four. Now divide out the coefficients. Multiply by six over ten to get x over y equals three over two. Check by putting x equal to three and y equal to two.

slides.heading: Quick check: dividendo
slides.body_md: Subtract, keep the second term.
slides.narration: Which property subtracts the second term from the first? Apply it to nine and four.

slides.heading: Worked example 3: the k-method
slides.body_md: If $a : b = c : d$, prove that $\dfrac{(a + b)^2}{(c + d)^2} = \dfrac{ab}{cd}$.
bullets: **Step 3 —** RHS $= \dfrac{bk \cdot b}{dk \cdot d} = \dfrac{b^2}{d^2}$, so LHS $=$ RHS.

visual.alt: Table testing the identity with numbers: with b equal to 3, d equal to 5 and k equal to 2, both sides equal 9 over 25; with b equal to 6, d equal to 9 and k equal to one third, both sides equal 4 over 9.
visual.caption: A numerical check is not a proof, but it catches slips.

slides.narration: Call the common value of the two ratios k. Then a is b k and c is d k. Substitute into both sides. The left side simplifies to b squared over d squared, and so does the right side. The table tests the result with numbers, which is a useful check but not a proof.

slides.heading: Worked example 4: an equation with square roots
slides.body_md: Solve $\dfrac{\sqrt{x + 4} + \sqrt{x - 4}}{\sqrt{x + 4} - \sqrt{x - 4}} = 2$.

visual.alt: Working table: componendo and dividendo gives root of x plus 4 over root of x minus 4 equals 3; squaring gives x plus 4 equals 9 times x minus 4, so 8x equals 40 and x equals 5; check: 3 plus 1 over 3 minus 1 equals 2.
visual.caption: Square only after the roots stand alone.

slides.narration: The sum and difference of two square roots is the signal for componendo and dividendo. It leaves one root over the other, equal to three. Now square both sides: x plus four equals nine times x minus four. So eight x is forty and x is five. Check by substituting.

slides.heading: Quick check: solve with the property
slides.body_md: Write $3$ as $\dfrac{3}{1}$ first.
slides.narration: Write the right side as three over one, apply componendo and dividendo, and solve for x.

slides.heading: Direct applications of proportion
slides.body_md: Many problems become a proportion: scales, recipes, changing ratios, numbers added to make a proportion.

nodes.label: Product of extremes $=$ product of means

visual.alt: Flow chart for a direct application: name the unknown, write the proportion, set the product of the extremes equal to the product of the means, solve, and check the answer in the original ratios.
visual.caption: Five steps for a direct application.

slides.narration: Many everyday problems hide a proportion. A map scale, a recipe for more people, or two numbers whose ratio changes. Name the unknown, write the proportion, use the product of extremes and means, solve, and always check the answer in the original ratios.

slides.heading: Worked example 5: making numbers proportional
slides.body_md: What number must be added to each of $3$, $6$, $7$ and $12$ so that they are in proportion?

visual.alt: Working table: the equation 3 plus x times 12 plus x equals 6 plus x times 7 plus x expands to 36 plus 15x equals 42 plus 13x, so x equals 3; the new numbers 6, 9, 10 and 15 have equal cross-products, 90.
visual.caption: The $x^2$ terms always cancel.

slides.narration: Let x be the number added. The new extremes are three plus x and twelve plus x; the new means are six plus x and seven plus x. Set the products equal. The x squared terms cancel, leaving two x equals six, so x is three. Check: six times fifteen and nine times ten are both ninety.

slides.heading: Worked example 6: a changing ratio
slides.body_md: Two numbers are in the ratio $2 : 5$. When $3$ is subtracted from each, the ratio becomes $1 : 4$. Find the numbers.

visual.alt: Table trying k from 2 to 5 for numbers 2k and 5k: after subtracting 3, k equal to 2 gives 1 to 7, k equal to 3 gives 3 to 12 which equals 1 to 4, k equal to 4 gives 5 to 17 and k equal to 5 gives 7 to 22. Only k equal to 3 works.
visual.caption: Only $k = 3$ gives $1 : 4$: the numbers are $6$ and $15$.

slides.narration: Write the numbers as two k and five k. After subtracting three, their ratio is one to four. Cross multiply: eight k minus twelve equals five k minus three, so k is three. The numbers are six and fifteen. The table shows that no other value of k works.

slides.heading: Quick check: a map scale
slides.body_md: Keep centimetres with centimetres.
slides.narration: Write the proportion with the map lengths on one side and the real distances on the other.

slides.heading: Summary
bullets: Invertendo, alternendo, componendo, dividendo, componendo and dividendo
C&D: sum over difference on both sides; it also works in reverse
Look for C&D when an equation is (sum) over (difference)
Applications: write the proportion, then product of extremes $=$ product of means

rows: $(a + b) : (a - b) = (c + d) : (c - d)$, and conversely
put $a = bk$, $c = dk$ to prove identities

visual.alt: Summary table for part 2: invertendo, alternendo, componendo, dividendo, and componendo and dividendo, which also works in reverse; and the k-method, putting a equal to b k and c equal to d k, for proving identities.
visual.caption: Part 2 on one card.

slides.narration: To sum up part two. One proportion gives invertendo, alternendo, componendo, dividendo, and componendo and dividendo. Use componendo and dividendo when you see a sum over a difference. Prove identities with the k method. In applications, write the proportion first and check your answer.

slides.heading: Exam tips: how marks are awarded
bullets: **C&D equation (3–4 marks):** property applied 1 + simplified 1 + answer 1 (+ check 1)
**Proof (3 marks):** substitution 1 + each side simplified 1 + conclusion 1
**Mistake:** applying C&D to one side only
**Mistake:** forgetting the negative square root when squares appear
**Mistake:** not dividing out coefficients when finding $x : y$
slides.narration: Name the property you use, because examiners give method marks for it. Apply componendo and dividendo to both sides at once. When you take a square root, think about the negative root too. In proofs, simplify each side separately and then conclude that they are equal.

sections.heading: 2. Proportion and the fourth proportional
sections.body_md:
Four numbers $a, b, c, d$ are **in proportion**, written $a : b = c : d$ or $a : b :: c : d$, when $\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{c}{d}$.

- $a$ and $d$ are the **extremes**; $b$ and $c$ are the **means**.
- **Test:** product of extremes $=$ product of means, $ad = bc$.
- $d$ is the **fourth proportional** to $a, b, c$: $d = \dfrac{bc}{a}$.

*Example:* $1.2, 2, 4.8, 8$ are in proportion since $1.2 \times 8 = 9.6 = 2 \times 4.8$; the fourth proportional to $5, 7, 15$ is $\dfrac{7 \times 15}{5} = 21$.

key_terms.definition_md: The first and fourth terms of a proportion.
The second and third terms of a proportion.
The number $x$ with $a : b = c : x$, that is $x = \dfrac{bc}{a}$.

formulas.latex: a : b = c : d \iff ad = bc
formulas.label: Test for proportion

visual.caption: In $4 : 7 = 12 : 21$, extremes $\times$ extremes $=$ means $\times$ means.

sections.heading: 3. Continued proportion, mean and third proportionals
sections.body_md:
$a, b, c$ are in **continued proportion** when $a : b = b : c$, so $b^2 = ac$.

- $b = \sqrt{ac}$ is the **mean proportional** between $a$ and $c$.
- $c = \dfrac{b^2}{a}$ is the **third proportional** to $a$ and $b$.
- $a, b, c, d$ are in continued proportion when $a : b = b : c = c : d$; then $a : d = a^3 : b^3$ (the triplicate ratio of $a : b$).

*Example:* the mean proportional between $0.32$ and $0.5$ is $\sqrt{0.16} = 0.4$; the third proportional to $5$ and $7.5$ is $\dfrac{56.25}{5} = 11.25$.

key_terms.definition_md: Three numbers with $a : b = b : c$, i.e. $b^2 = ac$.
The middle term $\sqrt{ac}$ of $a : b = b : c$.
The number $c = \dfrac{b^2}{a}$ with $a : b = b : c$.

visual.alt: Flow chart: a to b equals b to c gives b squared equals a times c; from this the mean proportional b is the square root of a c, and the third proportional c is b squared divided by a.
visual.caption: Continued proportion: one equation, two formulas.

visuals.alt: A rectangle 12 centimetres by 3 centimetres and a square of side 6 centimetres, drawn to the same scale. Both have area 36 square centimetres, so the side of the square, 6, is the mean proportional between 12 and 3.
visuals.caption: Equal areas: $12 \times 3 = 6 \times 6$, so $6$ is the mean proportional between $12$ and $3$.

visuals.caption: Both answers come from $b^2 = ac$.

sections.heading: 4. Invertendo and alternendo
sections.body_md:
If $a : b = c : d$, then

- **invertendo:** $b : a = d : c$ (invert both ratios);
- **alternendo:** $a : c = b : d$ (interchange the means).

Each new proportion still has equal cross-products, so it is a true proportion.

key_terms.definition_md: $a : b = c : d \Rightarrow b : a = d : c$.
$a : b = c : d \Rightarrow a : c = b : d$.

sections.heading: 5. Componendo, dividendo, and componendo and dividendo

key_terms.definition_md: $\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{c}{d} \Rightarrow \dfrac{a + b}{a - b} = \dfrac{c + d}{c - d}$, and conversely.

sections.heading: 6. Using the properties: equations, ratios and proofs
sections.body_md:
- **Equations:** when one side is (sum) $\div$ (difference), apply componendo and dividendo to both sides. *Example:* $\dfrac{2x + 9}{2x - 9} = \dfrac{5}{3}$ gives $\dfrac{4x}{18} = 4$, so $x = 18$.
- **Square roots:** $\dfrac{\sqrt{x + 4} + \sqrt{x - 4}}{\sqrt{x + 4} - \sqrt{x - 4}} = 2$ gives $\dfrac{\sqrt{x + 4}}{\sqrt{x - 4}} = 3$; square and solve: $x = 5$.
- **Finding a ratio:** $\dfrac{5x + 3y}{5x - 3y} = \dfrac{7}{3}$ gives $\dfrac{10x}{6y} = \dfrac{10}{4}$, so $x : y = 3 : 2$.
- **Proofs (k-method):** put $\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{c}{d} = k$, so $a = bk$, $c = dk$ (or $b = ak$, $c = ak^2$ for continued proportion), and simplify each side separately.

key_terms.definition_md: Writing every term through a common ratio $k$ (e.g. $a = bk$, $c = dk$) to prove a relation.

sections.heading: 7. Direct applications of proportion
sections.body_md:
Write the proportion, use product of extremes $=$ product of means, solve, and check in the original ratios.

- **Scales and recipes:** $3$ cm for $20$ km means $7.5$ cm stands for $\dfrac{20 \times 7.5}{3} = 50$ km.
- **Changing ratios:** numbers $2k$ and $5k$ with $3$ subtracted from each in the ratio $1 : 4$ give $k = 3$.
- **Making numbers proportional:** adding $3$ to each of $3, 6, 7, 12$ gives $6, 9, 10, 15$.
- **Areas and volumes:** areas of similar figures are in the duplicate ratio, and volumes of cubes in the triplicate ratio, of their lengths.

*Not in the ICSE 2027 syllabus:* applications of proportion beyond direct simple applications; this chapter keeps to direct ones.

notes.exam_tips_md:
**How marks are awarded**
- *Proportionals and kinds of ratio (1–2 marks):* proportion or rule written 1; answer in lowest terms 1.
- *Componendo and dividendo equation (3–4 marks):* property applied to both sides 1; simplified 1; answer 1; check 1.
- *Proof (3–4 marks):* substitution $a = bk$, $c = dk$ 1; each side simplified 1–2; conclusion 1.
- *10-mark structured question:* parts (a), (b), (c) usually 3 + 3 + 4; show all working.

**Common mistakes**
1. Doubling the terms instead of squaring them for a duplicate ratio.
2. Using the average instead of the mean proportional $\sqrt{ac}$.
3. Writing the third proportional in the wrong order ($b^2 \div a$, not $a^2 \div b$).
4. Calling alternendo invertendo, or applying componendo and dividendo to one side only.
5. Forgetting the negative square root when a ratio of squares appears.
6. Leaving coefficients in when finding $x : y$, or leaving a ratio unsimplified.

questions.solution_md: The duplicate ratio of $a : b$ is $a^2 : b^2$, so it is $5^2 : 7^2 = 25 : 49$. Option (b) only doubles each term, (c) is the sub-duplicate ratio and (d) the triplicate ratio.

questions.stem_md: Find the compound ratio of $2 : 3$, $9 : 10$ and $5 : 6$.
questions.solution_md: Multiply the first terms together and the second terms together: $(2 \times 9 \times 5) : (3 \times 10 \times 6) = 90 : 180 = 1 : 2$. Option (d) adds the terms instead of multiplying them.

questions.stem_md: The fourth proportional to $4$, $10$ and $6$ is

questions.solution_md: Mean proportional $= \sqrt{0.4 \times 8.1} = \sqrt{3.24} = 1.8$. Option (b) is the average of the two numbers, and (c) forgets the square root.

questions.stem_md: Find the third proportional to $6$ and $15$.
questions.solution_md: $6 : 15 = 15 : x$ gives $6x = 225$, so $x = 37.5$. Option (c) comes from the wrong order, $15 : 6 = 6 : x$.

questions.stem_md: From the proportion $p : q = r : s$ we conclude that $p : r = q : s$. Which property of proportion is used?
questions.solution_md: Alternendo interchanges the means: $a : b = c : d$ gives $a : c = b : d$. Invertendo would give $q : p = s : r$.

questions.stem_md: If $x : y = 9 : 4$, what is $(x - y) : y$?

questions.stem_md:

(b) Find the third proportional to $a - b$ and $a^2 - b^2$.

(a) Mean proportional $= \sqrt{2.5 \times 0.9} = \sqrt{2.25} = 1.5$.

(b) Let the third proportional be $x$: $(a - b) : (a^2 - b^2) = (a^2 - b^2) : x$.

$x = \dfrac{(a^2 - b^2)^2}{a - b} = \dfrac{(a - b)^2 (a + b)^2}{a - b} = (a - b)(a + b)^2$.

questions.stem_md: With the help of componendo and dividendo, solve the equation $\dfrac{3x + 4}{3x - 4} = \dfrac{9}{5}$.

answer.model_answer_md:
Componendo and dividendo:

$\dfrac{(3x + 4) + (3x - 4)}{(3x + 4) - (3x - 4)} = \dfrac{9 + 5}{9 - 5}$

$\dfrac{6x}{8} = \dfrac{14}{4}$, so $24x = 112$ and $x = \dfrac{14}{3}$.

questions.stem_md: If $a : b = c : d$, prove that $\dfrac{5a - 2b}{5a + 2b} = \dfrac{5c - 2d}{5c + 2d}$.

answer.model_answer_md:
Let $\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{c}{d} = k$, so $a = bk$ and $c = dk$.

LHS $= \dfrac{5bk - 2b}{5bk + 2b} = \dfrac{b(5k - 2)}{b(5k + 2)} = \dfrac{5k - 2}{5k + 2}$.

RHS $= \dfrac{5dk - 2d}{5dk + 2d} = \dfrac{d(5k - 2)}{d(5k + 2)} = \dfrac{5k - 2}{5k + 2}$.

So LHS $=$ RHS.

questions.solution_md: Use the k-method: put a = bk and c = dk, then simplify each side.

questions.stem_md: If $a$, $b$, $c$ are in continued proportion, prove that $\dfrac{a^2 + ab + b^2}{b^2 + bc + c^2} = \dfrac{a}{c}$.

answer.model_answer_md:
Let $\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{b}{c} = k$, so $b = ck$ and $a = bk = ck^2$.

LHS $= \dfrac{c^2k^4 + c^2k^3 + c^2k^2}{c^2k^2 + c^2k + c^2} = \dfrac{c^2k^2(k^2 + k + 1)}{c^2(k^2 + k + 1)} = k^2$.

RHS $= \dfrac{ck^2}{c} = k^2$, so LHS $=$ RHS.

questions.solution_md: Write a and b in terms of c and the common ratio k.

answer.model_answer_md:
Let the numbers be $5k$ and $9k$.

$\dfrac{5k - 4}{9k - 4} = \dfrac{3}{7}$, so $7(5k - 4) = 3(9k - 4)$.

$35k - 28 = 27k - 12$, so $8k = 16$ and $k = 2$.

The numbers are $10$ and $18$. Check: $6 : 14 = 3 : 7$.

questions.solution_md: Write the numbers as multiples of k, form the new proportion, and cross-multiply.

questions.stem_md: This equation contains square roots. Solve it for $x$ using componendo and dividendo: $\dfrac{\sqrt{x + 6} + \sqrt{x - 6}}{\sqrt{x + 6} - \sqrt{x - 6}} = 3$.

answer.model_answer_md:
Componendo and dividendo:

$\dfrac{2\sqrt{x + 6}}{2\sqrt{x - 6}} = \dfrac{3 + 1}{3 - 1} = 2$

Square both sides: $\dfrac{x + 6}{x - 6} = 4$, so $x + 6 = 4x - 24$.

$3x = 30$, so $x = 10$.

Check: $\sqrt{16} = 4$ and $\sqrt{4} = 2$, and $\dfrac{4 + 2}{4 - 2} = 3$.

questions.solution_md: Componendo and dividendo removes the sum and difference of the roots; then square and solve.

questions.stem_md: The two sides of this equation combine into perfect cubes. Solve it by componendo and dividendo: $\dfrac{x^3 + 3x}{3x^2 + 1} = \dfrac{189}{61}$.

answer.model_answer_md:
Componendo and dividendo:

$\dfrac{x^3 + 3x^2 + 3x + 1}{x^3 - 3x^2 + 3x - 1} = \dfrac{189 + 61}{189 - 61} = \dfrac{250}{128} = \dfrac{125}{64}$

$\dfrac{(x + 1)^3}{(x - 1)^3} = \dfrac{125}{64}$, so $\dfrac{x + 1}{x - 1} = \dfrac{5}{4}$ (taking cube roots).

Componendo and dividendo again: $\dfrac{2x}{2} = \dfrac{9}{1}$, so $x = 9$.

questions.solution_md: The sum and difference of the two sides are perfect cubes; take cube roots and apply the property again.

questions.stem_md: What number must be subtracted from each of $7$, $11$ and $23$ so that the results are in continued proportion? Then find the mean proportional between the new first and third numbers.

answer.model_answer_md:
Let $x$ be subtracted: $(11 - x)^2 = (7 - x)(23 - x)$.

$121 - 22x + x^2 = 161 - 30x + x^2$, so $8x = 40$ and $x = 5$.

The numbers become $2$, $6$ and $18$: $6^2 = 36 = 2 \times 18$.

Mean proportional between $2$ and $18$ $= \sqrt{36} = 6$.

questions.solution_md: For continued proportion the square of the middle term equals the product of the other two.

questions.stem_md: If $a : b = c : d$, prove that $\dfrac{a^2 + ab}{c^2 + cd} = \dfrac{b^2 - 2ab}{d^2 - 2cd}$.

answer.model_answer_md:
Let $\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{c}{d} = k$, so $a = bk$ and $c = dk$.

LHS $= \dfrac{b^2k^2 + b^2k}{d^2k^2 + d^2k} = \dfrac{b^2k(k + 1)}{d^2k(k + 1)} = \dfrac{b^2}{d^2}$.

RHS $= \dfrac{b^2 - 2b^2k}{d^2 - 2d^2k} = \dfrac{b^2(1 - 2k)}{d^2(1 - 2k)} = \dfrac{b^2}{d^2}$.

Hence LHS $=$ RHS.

questions.solution_md: Use the k-method and take out common factors on each side.

questions.stem_md: Two imagined water tanks are cubes whose edges are in the ratio $3 : 4$. Find (a) the ratio of the areas of their bases (b) the ratio of their volumes (c) the capacity of the larger tank, if the smaller one holds $5{,}400$ litres.

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Areas are in the duplicate ratio: $3^2 : 4^2 = 9 : 16$.

(b) Volumes are in the triplicate ratio: $3^3 : 4^3 = 27 : 64$.

(c) $27 : 64 = 5400 : x$, so $x = \dfrac{64 \times 5400}{27} = 12800$.

The larger tank holds $12{,}800$ litres.

questions.solution_md: Areas follow the duplicate ratio of the edges and volumes the triplicate ratio.

questions.stem_md: If $\dfrac{4m + 3n}{4m - 3n} = \dfrac{7}{4}$, use componendo and dividendo to find (a) $m : n$ (b) $(m + n) : (m - n)$.

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Componendo and dividendo: $\dfrac{8m}{6n} = \dfrac{7 + 4}{7 - 4} = \dfrac{11}{3}$.

$\dfrac{m}{n} = \dfrac{11}{3} \times \dfrac{6}{8} = \dfrac{11}{4}$, so $m : n = 11 : 4$.

(b) Componendo and dividendo on $\dfrac{m}{n} = \dfrac{11}{4}$: $\dfrac{m + n}{m - n} = \dfrac{11 + 4}{11 - 4} = \dfrac{15}{7}$.

So $(m + n) : (m - n) = 15 : 7$.

questions.solution_md: Apply the property once to find m : n, then again to the ratio m : n.

questions.stem_md:
Answer each part.

(a) Find the third proportional to $0.8$ and $2$, and the fourth proportional to $2.5$, $4$ and $7.5$.

(b) If $x : y = 3 : 4$, find $(5x - 2y) : (7x + 2y)$.

(c) Use the properties of proportion to solve $\dfrac{(x + 1)^2 - (x - 1)^2}{(x + 1)^2 + (x - 1)^2} = \dfrac{12}{13}$.

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Third proportional: $0.8 : 2 = 2 : x$, so $x = \dfrac{2 \times 2}{0.8} = 5$. Fourth proportional: $2.5 : 4 = 7.5 : y$, so $y = \dfrac{4 \times 7.5}{2.5} = 12$.

(b) Put $x = 3k$ and $y = 4k$: $(15k - 8k) : (21k + 8k) = 7k : 29k = 7 : 29$.

(c) Invertendo: $\dfrac{(x + 1)^2 + (x - 1)^2}{(x + 1)^2 - (x - 1)^2} = \dfrac{13}{12}$.

Componendo and dividendo: $\dfrac{2(x + 1)^2}{2(x - 1)^2} = \dfrac{13 + 12}{13 - 12} = 25$, so $\dfrac{x + 1}{x - 1} = 5$ or $\dfrac{x + 1}{x - 1} = -5$.

$x + 1 = 5x - 5$ gives $x = \dfrac{3}{2}$; $x + 1 = -5x + 5$ gives $x = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

Check for $x = \dfrac{3}{2}$: $\dfrac{6.25 - 0.25}{6.25 + 0.25} = \dfrac{6}{6.5} = \dfrac{12}{13}$.

questions.solution_md: Part (c): invert both sides first so that componendo and dividendo leaves a ratio of two squares; keep both square roots.

questions.stem_md:
Answer each part.

(a) The mean proportional between two numbers is $6$ and the third proportional to them is $48$. Find the numbers.

(b) If $a : b = c : d$, prove that $\dfrac{a^2 + 3b^2}{c^2 + 3d^2} = \dfrac{ab}{cd}$.

(c) Solve $\dfrac{\sqrt{3x + 4} + \sqrt{3x - 5}}{\sqrt{3x + 4} - \sqrt{3x - 5}} = 9$.

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Let the numbers be $a$ and $b$. Then $ab = 6^2 = 36$ and $\dfrac{b^2}{a} = 48$.

Multiplying, $b^3 = 36 \times 48 = 1728$, so $b = 12$ and $a = \dfrac{36}{12} = 3$. Check: $\sqrt{3 \times 12} = 6$ and $\dfrac{144}{3} = 48$.

(b) Let $a = bk$ and $c = dk$. LHS $= \dfrac{b^2k^2 + 3b^2}{d^2k^2 + 3d^2} = \dfrac{b^2(k^2 + 3)}{d^2(k^2 + 3)} = \dfrac{b^2}{d^2}$.

RHS $= \dfrac{bk \cdot b}{dk \cdot d} = \dfrac{b^2}{d^2}$, so LHS $=$ RHS.

(c) Componendo and dividendo: $\dfrac{2\sqrt{3x + 4}}{2\sqrt{3x - 5}} = \dfrac{9 + 1}{9 - 1} = \dfrac{5}{4}$.

Squaring: $\dfrac{3x + 4}{3x - 5} = \dfrac{25}{16}$, so $48x + 64 = 75x - 125$, $27x = 189$ and $x = 7$.

Check: $\sqrt{25} = 5$, $\sqrt{16} = 4$ and $\dfrac{5 + 4}{5 - 4} = 9$.

questions.solution_md: Part (a): multiply the two conditions to eliminate one number. Part (b): k-method. Part (c): componendo and dividendo, then square.

questions.stem_md:
Answer each part.

(a) Two numbers are in the ratio $3 : 5$. If $8$ is added to each, the ratio becomes $5 : 7$. Find the numbers.

(b) What number must be added to each of $5$, $11$, $19$ and $37$ so that the results are in proportion?

(c) An imagined village dairy has $66$ litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio $9 : 2$. (i) How much water must be added to make the ratio $3 : 1$? (ii) If instead milk is added, how much is needed to make the ratio $6 : 1$?

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Let the numbers be $3k$ and $5k$: $\dfrac{3k + 8}{5k + 8} = \dfrac{5}{7}$, so $21k + 56 = 25k + 40$, $4k = 16$ and $k = 4$. The numbers are $12$ and $20$; check: $20 : 28 = 5 : 7$.

(b) $(5 + x)(37 + x) = (11 + x)(19 + x)$ gives $185 + 42x = 209 + 30x$, so $12x = 24$ and $x = 2$.

The numbers become $7, 13, 21, 39$, and $7 \times 39 = 273 = 13 \times 21$.

(c) Milk $= \dfrac{9}{11} \times 66 = 54$ litres; water $= \dfrac{2}{11} \times 66 = 12$ litres.

(i) Add $w$ litres of water: $54 : (12 + w) = 3 : 1$, so $12 + w = 18$ and $w = 6$ litres.

(ii) Add $m$ litres of milk: $(54 + m) : 12 = 6 : 1$, so $54 + m = 72$ and $m = 18$ litres.

questions.solution_md: Each part turns a condition into a proportion and uses product of extremes = product of means; in (c) only one part of the mixture changes.

questions.stem_md:
Answer each part.

(a) Find $x$ if $(x + 1) : (x + 5) = (x + 4) : (x + 12)$, and verify the proportion.

(b) If $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ are in continued proportion, prove that $a : d$ is the triplicate ratio of $a : b$.

(c) Use componendo and dividendo to find $p : q$ if $\dfrac{p^3 + q^3}{p^3 - q^3} = \dfrac{65}{63}$, and hence find $(p + q) : (p - q)$.

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Product of extremes = product of means: $(x + 1)(x + 12) = (x + 5)(x + 4)$.

$x^2 + 13x + 12 = x^2 + 9x + 20$, so $4x = 8$ and $x = 2$. The terms are $3, 7, 6, 14$, and $3 \times 14 = 42 = 7 \times 6$.

(b) Let $\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{b}{c} = \dfrac{c}{d} = k$, so $c = dk$, $b = dk^2$ and $a = dk^3$. Then $\dfrac{a}{d} = \dfrac{dk^3}{d} = k^3$.

Also $\dfrac{a^3}{b^3} = k^3$, because $\dfrac{a}{b} = k$. So $a : d = a^3 : b^3$, the triplicate ratio of $a : b$.

(c) Componendo and dividendo: $\dfrac{2p^3}{2q^3} = \dfrac{65 + 63}{65 - 63} = \dfrac{128}{2} = 64$, so $\dfrac{p}{q} = 4$ (cube root) and $p : q = 4 : 1$.

Componendo and dividendo on $\dfrac{p}{q} = \dfrac{4}{1}$: $\dfrac{p + q}{p - q} = \dfrac{4 + 1}{4 - 1} = \dfrac{5}{3}$, so $(p + q) : (p - q) = 5 : 3$.

questions.solution_md: Part (a): cross-multiply; the squares cancel. Part (b): express every term through d and k. Part (c): take a cube root after the first use of the property.

questions.stem_md:
Answer each part.

(a) Find the compound ratio of the duplicate ratio of $2 : 3$ and the sub-duplicate ratio of $81 : 16$.

(b) If $b$ is the mean proportional between $a$ and $c$, prove that $(a + b + c)(a - b + c) = a^2 + b^2 + c^2$.

(c) Use componendo and dividendo to solve $\dfrac{x^3 + 27x}{9x^2 + 27} = \dfrac{35}{19}$.

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Duplicate ratio of $2 : 3$ is $4 : 9$; sub-duplicate ratio of $81 : 16$ is $9 : 4$. Compound ratio $= (4 \times 9) : (9 \times 4) = 36 : 36 = 1 : 1$.

(b) Since $b$ is the mean proportional, $b^2 = ac$. LHS $= (a + c + b)(a + c - b) = (a + c)^2 - b^2$.

$= a^2 + 2ac + c^2 - b^2 = a^2 + 2b^2 + c^2 - b^2 = a^2 + b^2 + c^2 =$ RHS.

(c) Componendo and dividendo: $\dfrac{x^3 + 9x^2 + 27x + 27}{x^3 - 9x^2 + 27x - 27} = \dfrac{35 + 19}{35 - 19} = \dfrac{54}{16} = \dfrac{27}{8}$.

So $\dfrac{(x + 3)^3}{(x - 3)^3} = \dfrac{27}{8}$ and $\dfrac{x + 3}{x - 3} = \dfrac{3}{2}$; then $2x + 6 = 3x - 9$, so $x = 15$.

Check: $\dfrac{3375 + 405}{2025 + 27} = \dfrac{3780}{2052} = \dfrac{35}{19}$.

questions.solution_md: Part (b): pair a + c and use b² = ac. Part (c): the numerator and denominator combine into the cubes of x + 3 and x − 3.

questions.stem_md:
Answer each part.

(a) If $a : b = c : d$, use the properties of proportion to prove that $(a + 2b) : (a - 2b) = (c + 2d) : (c - 2d)$.

(b) If $a : b = 3 : 2$, find $(2a^2 + b^2) : (2a^2 - b^2)$.

(c) If $\dfrac{2a + 3b}{2a - 3b} = \dfrac{2c + 3d}{2c - 3d}$, prove that $a : b = c : d$. Hence find $c$ when $a = 6$, $b = 9$ and $d = 12$.

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) $\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{c}{d}$; multiplying both sides by $\dfrac{1}{2}$ gives $\dfrac{a}{2b} = \dfrac{c}{2d}$. Componendo and dividendo: $\dfrac{a + 2b}{a - 2b} = \dfrac{c + 2d}{c - 2d}$.

(b) $\dfrac{a^2}{b^2} = \dfrac{9}{4}$, so $\dfrac{2a^2}{b^2} = \dfrac{18}{4} = \dfrac{9}{2}$.

Componendo and dividendo: $\dfrac{2a^2 + b^2}{2a^2 - b^2} = \dfrac{9 + 2}{9 - 2} = \dfrac{11}{7}$, so the ratio is $11 : 7$.

(c) Componendo and dividendo: $\dfrac{(2a + 3b) + (2a - 3b)}{(2a + 3b) - (2a - 3b)} = \dfrac{(2c + 3d) + (2c - 3d)}{(2c + 3d) - (2c - 3d)}$, that is $\dfrac{4a}{6b} = \dfrac{4c}{6d}$.

Multiplying both sides by $\dfrac{3}{2}$: $\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{c}{d}$, so $a : b = c : d$.

With $a = 6$, $b = 9$, $d = 12$: $6 : 9 = c : 12$, so $c = \dfrac{6 \times 12}{9} = 8$.

questions.solution_md: Parts (a) and (b): bring the ratio to the form needed, then apply componendo and dividendo. Part (c): the property works in reverse as well.

questions.stem_md:
Answer each part.

(a) An imagined school garden has a rectangular bed $25$ m long and $9$ m wide. Find the side of a square bed with the same area, and show that it is the mean proportional between the length and the breadth.

(b) The present ages of Meera and her uncle are in the ratio $3 : 8$. In $12$ years' time the ratio will be $1 : 2$. Find their present ages.

(c) On an imagined trekking map, $4$ cm represents $6$ km. (i) What actual distance does $11$ cm represent? (ii) A lake has an actual area of $27$ km². What is its area on the map?

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Area $= 25 \times 9 = 225$ m², so the square has side $\sqrt{225} = 15$ m. Since $25 : 15 = 15 : 9$ (both equal $5 : 3$), $15$ is the mean proportional between $25$ and $9$.

(b) Let the ages be $3k$ and $8k$ years: $\dfrac{3k + 12}{8k + 12} = \dfrac{1}{2}$, so $6k + 24 = 8k + 12$, $2k = 12$ and $k = 6$.

Meera is $18$ years old and her uncle is $48$; check: $30 : 60 = 1 : 2$.

(c)(i) $4 : 6 = 11 : x$, so $x = \dfrac{6 \times 11}{4} = 16.5$ km.

(ii) Areas are in the duplicate ratio of lengths: map area : actual area $= 4^2 : 6^2 = 16 : 36$ (cm² to km²).

$16 : 36 = y : 27$, so $y = \dfrac{16 \times 27}{36} = 12$ cm².

questions.solution_md: Part (a): mean proportional as the side of an equal square. Part (b): ages as multiples of k. Part (c): lengths scale in the given ratio, areas in its duplicate ratio.
